evidence.quote: Our argument combines Popa’s free-independence construction in tracial ultraproducts (Popa 1995, 2014) [[Popa1995](#ref-Popa1995), [Popa2014](#ref-Popa2014)] with a perturbation whose effect accumulates along a long word.

requires_concepts: Baire category theorem on the unitary group

prerequisites.concept: Single generation of separable-predual type II_1 factors

evidence.quote: Relative generation then gives four self-adjoint generators for every separable-predual $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor.

outputs.exact_statement: Let $P\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors, with $M$ of separable predual. The set $$\{u\in\mathcal U(M):W^*(P,u)=M\}$$ is a dense $G_\delta$ subset of the unitary group $\mathcal U(M)$ for the trace $2$-norm topology.
Every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $M$ with separable predual is generated by two self-adjoint elements. Equivalently, there is an $x\in M$ such that $M=W^*(x)$.
The inclusion $\mathbf Q\subset\mathbf M$ is irreducible: $$\mathbf Q'\cap\mathbf M=\mathbb C1.$$

Let $P\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors, and put $\mathbf Q=P^\omega\subset M^\omega=\mathbf M$. For every linear subspace $X\subset\mathbf M$ that is separable in $2$-norm and satisfies $\tau(x)=0$ for all $x\in X$, there is a diffuse abelian von Neumann algebra $A\subset\mathbf Q$ such that $$\label{eq:popa-independence}
  \tau(x_0a_1x_1\cdots a_mx_m)=0$$ whenever $m\geq1$, $x_0\in X\cup\{1\}$, $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in X$, and $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in A$ have trace zero.

Let $D\subset\mathbf M$ be a norm-separable unital $C^*$-algebra. There is a Haar unitary $t\in\mathbf Q$ free from $D$. In particular, $$\label{eq:free-endpoints}
  \tau(d_0t^{n_1}d_1\cdots t^{n_j}d_j)=0$$ for every $j\geq1$, every $n_1,\ldots,n_j\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, and all $d_0,\ldots,d_j\in D$ such that $\tau(d_i)=0$ for $1\leq i\leq j-1$. The two endpoints $d_0,d_j$ are arbitrary.

Let $D$ be a unital $C^*$-subalgebra of a finite tracial von Neumann algebra, and let $t$ be a Haar unitary free from $D$. If $a,b\in\mathcal U(D)$, then both $atb$ and $t^*$ are Haar unitaries free from $D$. Both satisfy [eq:free-endpoints] in place of $t$.

Let $F$ be a free group with a specified free basis, let $\mathcal L$ be the set of basis elements and their inverses, and let $\lambda$ be the left regular representation on $\ell^2(F)$. For every finitely supported family $(b_\gamma)_{\gamma\in\mathcal L}$, $$\lVert \sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal L}b_\gamma\lambda(\gamma)\rVert
  \le 2\left(\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal L}|b_\gamma|^2\right)^{1/2}.$$

Let $P\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. Given $u,z\in\mathcal U(M)$, $\xi\in M$, and $0<\alpha<1/2$, for every integer $\ell\ge1$ there are $\widetilde u\in\mathcal U(M)$ and $\widetilde t_0,\ldots,\widetilde t_\ell\in\mathcal U(P)$ such that, with $$\widetilde W=\widetilde t_0
     \prod_{k=1}^{\ell}(\widetilde u\,\widetilde t_k),$$ one has $$\label{eq:perturbation-bounds}
\begin{aligned}
  \lVert \widetilde u-u\rVert_2
    &\le \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{2\ell}}+\frac1\ell,\\
  \left|\tau(\xi^*\widetilde W)
           -\frac\alpha2\tau(\xi^*z)\right|
    &\le \lVert \xi\rVert_2\frac{4\alpha^2}{1-2\alpha}+\frac1\ell.
\end{aligned}$$ All products indexed by $k$ are taken in increasing order from left to right. The unitaries may depend on $\ell$.
The Hilbert space $L^2(M,\tau)$ is separable, and $\mathcal U(M)$ is complete for the metric $d(u,v)=\lVert u-v\rVert_2$.

Each $f_\xi$ is bounded and lower semicontinuous on $(\mathcal U(M),d)$. There is a dense $G_\delta$ subset $\mathcal C\subset\mathcal U(M)$ such that every $f_\xi$, $\xi\in L^2(M,\tau)$, is continuous at every point of $\mathcal C$.
Let $N\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors with separable preduals. There is a hyperfinite $\mathrm{II}_1$ subfactor $R\subset N$ such that $R'\cap M=\mathbb C1$.
The hyperfinite $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with separable predual is generated by two self-adjoint elements.
Every $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with separable predual is generated by four self-adjoint elements.
If a unital von Neumann algebra $N$ is generated by four self-adjoint elements, then $M_2(N)$ is generated by two self-adjoint elements.

For every integer $n\geq3$, the factor $L(\mathbb F_n)$ with its canonical trace has two finite self-adjoint generating tuples on which both $\delta$ and $\delta_0$ take different values. In particular, neither dimension is determined by the generated tracial von Neumann algebra.
